Assemble block draws into one array

Source: R/assemble.R
indri_assemble_draws.Rd

Combines the per-block draws (posterior draws, or the REML engines' normal draws) into a K by K by D array. fit_G() uses "mixture"; the default here is "average" only for backward compatibility. Either way the result carries block-level uncertainty through; it is not a posterior over the joint matrix, because subsets share traits and data and are therefore dependent. See NOTES.md.

Usage

indri_assemble_draws(
  draws,
  subsets,
  K = NULL,
  method = c("average", "mixture"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

draws

List of s by s by D arrays, one per subset.

subsets

Integer matrix of trait indices, one subset per row.

K

Number of traits; inferred from subsets when NULL, which is only right when the subsets happen to reach the last trait.

method

"average" or "mixture"; see Details. Use "mixture" for intervals: "average" is overconfident.

seed

Optional seed for the block choice in "mixture". The caller's random state is left untouched.

Value

A K by K by D array. Entries no subset covers are 0 for "average" and NA for "mixture".

Details

method = "average" averages draw d across every block that covers an entry, exactly as the means are averaged. Because the block chains are independent, this shrinks the spread of an entry covered c times by about 1 / sqrt(c), while the block estimates themselves, fitted to the same individuals, have nearly perfectly correlated errors: the band is too narrow and gets narrower the better a pair is covered.

method = "mixture" instead takes each entry of draw d from one covering block chosen at random, so an entry's draws are a mixture of its block posteriors: the spread is the average within-block spread plus the spread between blocks. Entries are drawn independently of one another, so a mixed covariance draw need not be positive semi-definite; mix per-block correlation draws (pass them as draws) when correlations are the target.

Examples

# Illustrative draws for the same two-trait subset from two block fits.
subsets <- rbind(c(1, 2), c(1, 2))
make_draws <- function(correlations) {
  array(unlist(lapply(correlations, function(r)
    matrix(c(1, r, r, 1), 2))), dim = c(2, 2, length(correlations)))
}
draws <- list(make_draws(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4)),
              make_draws(c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8)))
averaged <- indri_assemble_draws(draws, subsets)
mixed <- indri_assemble_draws(draws, subsets, method = "mixture")
averaged[1, 2, ]
#> [1] 0.3 0.4 0.5 0.6
mixed[1, 2, ]
#> [1] 0.5 0.2 0.3 0.8
# Mixture entries are pointwise draws, not a joint PSD matrix posterior.
